messages:
alex_support: Hey team — customer Julia reporting SSE streams that start fine but then stop mid-response after ~20–40s. They see partial chunks (last token truncated) and then a disconnect. Logs on our frontend show repeated `write EAGAIN` followed by `EPIPE` when we try to flush. Request id: req_01HXXY.
customer_julia: Adding context: this happens only when our app runs behind our corp proxy (BlueGate). Direct mobile connections work. We also noticed spikes in our billing metrics because our client library retries 4x quickly.
alex_support: Repro steps from customer (copied):
1) Use Node fetch with keep-alive agent behind corporate proxy
2) Connect to /v1/stream with Authorization: Bearer <token>
3) Receive 1–2 SSE events, then partial line then stream closes. No 4xx returned by API prior to close.
customer_julia: Token is short-lived; we also do silent refresh at ~55min in other flows but here the failures happen immediately on connect.
maria_oncall: Noted. I pulled recent runtime logs — here's the excerpt: 
```
2026-11-09T14:12:08.223Z INFO stream:start req=req_01HXXY client_ip=10.12.8.4
2026-11-09T14:12:28.451Z WARN runtime:socket_write write_errno=11 (EAGAIN) bytes_pending=65536 req=req_01HXXY
2026-11-09T14:12:28.452Z WARN runtime:socket_write backpressure=true req=req_01HXXY
2026-11-09T14:12:28.459Z ERROR runtime:socket_write write_errno=32 (EPIPE) req=req_01HXXY
2026-11-09T14:12:28.460Z INFO stream:end reason=client-reset req=req_01HXXY
```
cheng_runtime: Those bytes_pending numbers look like the socket send buffer saturated (64KB). Could be proxy buffering entire response then dropping the socket when timeout/limit hit. Nginx/BlueGate often buffers by default.
alex_support: Customer tested with curl (direct) and it stays open; behind proxy it fails. They provided the proxy config snippet: `proxy_buffering on; proxy_buffers 8 64k; proxy_busy_buffers_size 128k; proxy_read_timeout 30s;`
cheng_runtime: That proxy_read_timeout 30s aligns with the 20–40s observed. When the backend is streaming and client is a slow consumer or the proxy imposes a timer, writes block and our runtime eventually gets EAGAIN then EPIPE.
customer_julia: Any immediate mitigations we can try?
maria_oncall: Quick mitigation options — test these one at a time: 
- Disable proxy_buffering for SSE routes (`proxy_buffering off;`) so proxy streams bytes immediately.
- Lower chunk sizes from server to keep kernel send buffer moving (we currently flush at ~16KB). Try flushing every 2–4KB.
- Add periodic keep-alive comment lines (":\n") every 10s to prevent proxy idle timeouts.
- On client: increase socket read window / accept larger buffers; avoid synchronous blocking processing on main thread.
cheng_runtime: Longer-term: update runtime to detect persistent EAGAINs and gracefully throttle generation or fall back to smaller chunked writes. Also add an opt-in header `x-sse-no-buffer: 1` to signal proxies to disable buffering (we can document this).
alex_support: We also saw billing spikes — customer client retried on connection close and hit rate limits then retried again. We should add guidance to: exponential backoff with jitter for reconnects and inspect for HTTP 401/403 before retrying.
customer_julia: Regarding auth: one of our earlier traces showed a token rotate returned a 401 on reconnect; client immediately attempted to re-open without refreshing token, then got 401 repeatedly. That triggered 4 quick reconnect attempts within 10s.
maria_oncall: Support checklist I'm doing now: 
- Enabled diagnostic logging for the customer's req ids and filtered for EAGAIN/EPIPE.
- Asked customer to try `curl -N` through their proxy to see streaming keep-alives.
- Suggested nginx `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_set_header Connection '';` for SSE path.
- Suggested client to implement token refresh on 401 rather than blind reconnect.
cheng_runtime: I pushed a small instrumentation change to runtime to capture per-socket pending bytes and emit a metric `sse.socket.backpressure` with tags {proxy,region}. Pushed to canary in us-west-2. Deploy-bot: canary deploy started for service/runtime@canary-20261109-2.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: service/runtime@canary-20261109-2 — rolling 2 nodes.
alex_support: Customer tried `proxy_buffering off` and reported improvement — stream stays open longer but still sometimes drops if their client is paused for long. We recommended adding keep-alive comments and smaller flushes.
customer_julia: After changing buffer settings and adding keep-alives, we saw no further EAGAINs in last 6 tests. Billing spike stopped when we added exponential backoff on reconnects. Thanks!
cheng_runtime: Follow-ups: 
- We'll add docs for SSE best-practices behind proxies (nginx, BlueGate, corp proxies).
- Engineer action item: implement a soft-fallback on sustained write EAGAIN to reduce chunk size or pause generation to let client catch up.
- Security/product: validate `x-sse-no-buffer` header semantics; ensure it can't be abused for cache-bypass.
alex_support: Closing loop with customer; tagging this thread for knowledgebase article. End notes: reproduction commands we gave to customer: 
```
# curl (direct)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream"

# curl via proxy (simulate corporate proxy)
curl -N -x http://localhost:3128 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream"

# Node fetch example
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const agent = new (require('http')).Agent({ keepAlive: true });
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` }, agent })
  .then(res => res.body.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk)));
```
alex_support: Adding this to support KB draft under "SSE behind corporate proxies". Closing thread.
